item.title: 'Receiving necessary medical attention': Embassy updates on Indian Flydubai pilot
item.description: A flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv experienced a serious incident that required an emergency landing. Following a cockpit altercation, one pilot was arrested and investigated by Saudi authorities. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu confirmed the situation was managed and the safety of passengers was prioritized. Warplanes were scrambled in response to potential hijacking fears but were later stood down.
item.dc:creator: YASHASVI VASISTHA

item.title: Bombs without brakes? US-China AI race may be harder to control than the nuclear one
item.description: The people building artificial intelligence keep reaching for the same comparison. Billionaire Elon Musk has called AI “far more dangerous than nukes.” Anthropic boss Dario Amodei describes the most powerful models as “weaponisable nuclear materials.” Sam Altman, when asked how AI could be policed, often points to the International Atomic Energy Agency(IAEA), the world's nuclear watchdog.
item.dc:creator: RAJEEV SINGH

item.title: Trump announces $200bn South Korean investment in US, $54bn for Alaska LNG
item.description: South Korea is making waves with a monumental commitment of $200 billion toward US energy endeavors. This ambitious plan encompasses a critical liquefied natural gas project in Alaska and a gas-fired power facility in Texas. Moreover, investments in eight nuclear reactors across the nation are also underway. These strategic ventures stem from a $350 billion trade agreement signed in November 2025, reinforcing economic cooperation between South Korea and the US.
item.dc:creator: VIJAYA SRIVASTAVA

item.title: In 2018, Musk gave $480,350 for Flint school filters; students drink from fountains
item.description: Flint Community Schools has installed new water filtration systems across its schools and administrative building. Students were previously reliant on bottled water for drinking due to contamination concerns. Testing confirmed that the new systems effectively removed lead and harmful bacteria from the water supply. Although drinking stations are now available, bottled water will continue to be provided throughout the school year.

item.description: The money changes include a reduction in the number of free ATM transactions for certain State Bank of India (SBI) salary account customers, new disclosure norms for interest rates on bulk fixed deposits (FDs), revised charges under the National Pension System (NPS) and mandatory Aadhaar authentication for receiving LPG subsidies.
item.dc:creator: TOI BUSINESS DESK

item.title: After two Asian Games medals, Harita Bhadra sets her sights on 22.45s and World Championships
item.description: Harita Bhadra arrived at the Asian Games chasing a podium finish and left Nagoya with two bronze medals, in the women’s 200m and mixed 4x100m relay. Her first senior international competition has also sharpened the next target: a 22.45-second run, the qualifying mark for the 2027 World Championships. Bhadra reflects on the races, the mental lessons from Nagoya, her relay experience and why she believes the next level is within reach.
item.dc:creator: VINEET RAMAKRISHNAN

item.title: Iowa developer's $11M mall plan stalled by 50-year-old JCPenney lease
item.description: Threshold Capital has acquired the Valley West Mall property for $11 million in West Des Moines, Iowa. This ambitious mixed-use development aims to blend residential, retail, and entertainment spaces. Yet, they must navigate a challenging lease agreement with JCPenney that could impede progress. City officials are contemplating up to $110 million in public funding for this expansive project, with hopes of commencing construction following city approvals and finalized site plans.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: 1,000+ acre Loudoun estate with Potomac frontage listed for $41.5M
item.description: More than 1,000 acres of protected Northern Virginia countryside in Loudoun County are listed for $41.575 million. The offering includes Potomac River frontage, vineyards, farmland and a historic 1700s house across two tracts. The land has been placed under conservation easements, while the properties offer potential for residential, agricultural and hospitality uses.
item.dc:creator: TOI REAL ESTATE DESK

item.title: Michael & Susan Dell’s Foundation pledges $36.6 million for 1,400 Austin homes
item.description: Michael & Susan Dell Foundation has committed $36.6 million to expand Community First! Village in Austin. The expansion aims to accommodate up to 1,900 residents experiencing chronic homelessness while adding 127 acres to the site. Infrastructure work is expected to begin in 2023 across properties along Hog Eye Road and Burleson Road. This development is part of a broader campaign to support affordable and permanent housing needs.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Rare blue-eyed white tiger Tejas travels 550 km to become Dehradun Zoo star
item.description: Dehradun Zoo has announced the arrival of Tejas, a magnificent white tiger from Gwalior Zoo. To ensure his well-being, Tejas will undergo a 20-day quarantine for careful observation. The zoo is dedicated to wildlife education and conservation, enticing visitors with outdoor experiences. After quarantine, Tejas will share his habitat with Bhola, the Royal Bengal tiger, offering wildlife enthusiasts an opportunity to explore the beauty of nature.
item.dc:creator: TOI LIFESTYLE DESK

item.title: Is it time for Congress and INDIA bloc to take a leaf out of CJP's playbook?
item.description: The INDIA bloc, under Congress's leadership, is gearing up for a vigorous campaign against electoral misconduct and the Election Commission's authority. Their strategy includes widespread protests and a pivotal 'Save Democracy March' to elevate public consciousness while pressuring for essential reforms. Additionally, the bloc intends to approach the Supreme Court about ongoing electoral challenges. Among their key proposals are reinstating ballot voting and refining voter registration methods.
item.dc:creator: KUNAL VARMA

item.title: Ronaldo leaves Portugal camp, promises truth 'in due time', wishes team-mates luck
item.description: Cristiano Ronaldo has left Portugal’s camp ahead of Thursday’s Nations League clash with Denmark following a dispute over his role under new head coach Jorge Jesus. Ronaldo confirmed his departure after Jesus said he would not start the match. The 41-year-old has not announced his international retirement, but said he would reveal the reasons for his decision “in due time.”
item.dc:creator: SOROR SHAIZA

item.title: 'The Paradise' BO day 7: Nani's actioner sees 22.7% drop; net reaches Rs 104.90 cr
item.description: Facing a downturn, 'The Paradise' recorded Rs 3.40 crore net in India on its seventh day. The Indian total now stands at Rs 104.90 crore, while the global gross reaches Rs 154.80 crore. The Telugu edition was responsible for Rs 2.65 crore of Day 7's revenue, primarily driven by Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, which provided Rs 2.85 crore.

item.title: He built device to make drinking water from air; 3 years later, won Chemistry Nobel
item.description: Omar Yaghi’s innovative team has created a groundbreaking device that pulls water from the atmosphere under adverse conditions. Employing a specialized metal-organic framework, their technology functions independently of electric power. Yaghi’s personal journey significantly shaped his commitment to tackling water scarcity. Their remarkable achievements earned them the Nobel Prize in Chemistry, and future expansions may enhance the reach of this technology.

item.title: 'It was like a horror film': How Flydubai pilot was restrained with headphones
item.description: An Israeli passenger recounted how he and others restrained a co-pilot trying to take control of a flydubai flight. The incident started when a struggle was heard in the cockpit and quickly escalated. After the pilot was attacked, the plane nosedived, prompting passengers to spring into action. They managed to stabilize the aircraft while using headphones to restrain the co-pilot.

item.title: Senior citizen wrongly paid tax on Rs 25.42L interest; ITAT orders Rs 9.91L refund
item.description: Each year, the senior citizen reported the interest earned from his investments in tax-free bonds under the ‘exempt income’ category in his income tax return (ITR). But made a mistake in one year. The man realised the error only after the deadline for filing a revised ITR had passed. He therefore approached the jurisdictional assessing officer (JAO) and filed a rectification application.
item.dc:creator: TOI BUSINESS DESK

item.title: US troops finally leave Iraq 23 years after Saddam’s fall
item.description: The withdrawal of US troops from Iraq signifies a pivotal change in the nation’s security landscape. As Iraq assumes full control over its safety and counterterrorism strategies, the Kurdistan Region confronts obstacles from diminished American military backing amid rising regional tensions. Meanwhile, Baghdad aims to strengthen its authority over various armed factions while navigating intricate political issues.

item.title: 'I grabbed the terrorist': Flydubai passenger tells Netanyahu how he subdued pilot
item.description: A harrowing experience unfolded on a flydubai flight as an Israeli passenger detailed his brave actions in subduing an assailant in the cockpit. The flight, destined for Tel Aviv from Dubai, was forced to divert to Saudi Arabia due to the alarming situation. The passengers' quick response helped manage the emergency, preventing what could have been a catastrophic hijacking.

item.title: UAE planning to develop shipping alternatives, port that bypasses Hormuz
item.description: L'imad Holding from Abu Dhabi is planning to heighten its infrastructure investments beyond the Strait of Hormuz. This strategic shift aims to reduce the emirate's reliance on this pivotal waterway amid current regional turbulence. Development plans focus on enhancing port infrastructure in Fujairah, ensuring stable routes for oil and other essential goods. However, security threats still pose challenges to Gulf infrastructure, complicating these investment efforts.
item.dc:creator: PRANJAL PANDEY

item.title: Mother and nominee son died; bank delayed funds to father, ordered to pay Rs 15,000
item.description: A woman had Rs 62,541 in her savings account. Her son was registered as the nominee. Both the mother and son passed away, leaving her 83-year-old husband as the only surviving member of the family. The man was a farmer and was not very familiar with English.
